meta.description: Analyze single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac/ArchR (R) and SnapATAC2 (Python alternative), including QC, TF-IDF/LSI, differential accessibility, and chromVAR motif deviation analysis.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported values came from the synthetic audit object or direct capability checks and are labeled as such.

practice_boundaries.detail: The tested outputs make no diagnostic or treatment claims and retain the Skill's research-only interpretation boundaries.

methodological_ground.detail: The executed workflow uses depth-aware DA and retains warnings about circular peak calling, motif-family ambiguity, and gene activity limits.

code_usability.detail: The exact documented invocation of scripts/run_chromvar.R fails before analysis with 'there is no package called Signac' because the script does not add the designated environment's private R library to .libPaths().

functional_suitability.note: Core Signac workflow is strong, but the opening workflow still names removed RunChromVAR() and the advertised chromVAR script fails as invoked.

reliability.note: Seeded chromVAR design and many caveats are sound, but the runnable script omits the environment library initialization required by the stated audit runtime.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md remains compact, with detailed chromVAR logic moved to a dedicated script.

agent_usability.note: Decision tables and common errors are useful, but a prominent stale wrapper name and a failing documented command create avoidable agent trial-and-error.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers, quick starts, and version guidance are clear; explicit out-of-scope handoff guidance remains limited.

security.note: No credentials, raw-code execution, destructive commands, or unnecessary sensitive-data handling were found.

maintainability.note: The dedicated script is modular, but it duplicates critical runtime assumptions instead of declaring the required library path itself.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision and deterministic seeding are good; the missing direct-run environment setup and limited escape hatches reduce reliable autonomous use.

inputs.label: Signac TF-IDF/LSI and depth diagnosis
inputs.note: Executed on the archived audit's synthetic 270-cell, 222-peak Signac object; the fresh audit-owned LSI run found depth-correlated components 1 and 3 and wrote core_lsi.rds.
inputs.execution_note: run/01_inspect_object.R and run/02_core_lsi.R executed through the designated r.sh wrapper; 50 LSI dimensions, components 1 and 3 dropped, 28 dimensions retained.

assertions.text: TF-IDF and SVD complete on the supplied Signac object
assertions.note: run/02_core_lsi.R completed and wrote core_lsi.rds.

assertions.text: Depth correlation is assessed per component rather than by a positional default
assertions.note: The fresh run calculated correlations for all 50 dimensions and selected components 1 and 3.

assertions.text: A usable downstream neighbor graph is produced
assertions.note: FindNeighbors and FindClusters completed on retained dimensions.

assertions.text: Raw-fragment QC is re-executed from the canonical input
assertions.note: The retained synthetic object is already QC-annotated; this final pass re-executed LSI rather than reconstructing raw-fragment QC.

inputs.label: Framework selection for a large atlas
inputs.note: The direct Mode-A response selected an on-disk or matrix-free alternative rather than in-memory Signac for a 500,000-nucleus request and named cross-ecosystem lossiness.
inputs.execution_note: run/04_tool_availability.ps1 executed: ArchR, SnapATAC2, and MACS3 are absent in the designated Windows environment, matching TOOLS.md; the decision-table response did not claim local execution.

assertions.text: The framework recommendation respects the stated scalability limits
assertions.note: The response directs a very large atlas away from in-memory Signac.

assertions.text: The response distinguishes ArchR and SnapATAC2 operating models
assertions.note: It identifies on-disk HDF5 versus backed AnnData/matrix-free spectral analysis.

assertions.text: The response warns about lossy R-to-Python round trips
assertions.note: The Skill explicitly states that ChromatinAssay and ArchR structures do not round-trip.

assertions.text: Unavailable local tools are not represented as executed
assertions.note: Capability script confirmed all three alternate-tool checks are false.

inputs.label: Multiple depth-correlated LSI components
inputs.note: The fresh run actually found two depth-correlated components, validating the Skill's requirement to inspect every component rather than mechanically omitting LSI_1.
inputs.execution_note: run/02_core_lsi.R executed and reported drop=1,3; the response retained only dimensions not exceeding the absolute correlation threshold.

assertions.text: Every LSI component is evaluated for depth correlation
assertions.note: The script applies cor() over every embedding column.

assertions.text: All flagged components are excluded
assertions.note: Both components 1 and 3 were removed.

assertions.text: The response does not impose dims=2:30 blindly
assertions.note: Selection is data-derived.

assertions.text: The analysis remains within scATAC exploratory scope
assertions.note: No individual-level or clinical inference was made.

inputs.label: Depth-aware differential accessibility
inputs.note: A logistic-regression FindMarkers run on groups 0 and 1 wrote 147 rows, including 55 adjusted-significant peaks.
inputs.execution_note: run/03_da_markers.R executed through r.sh against obj_qc.rds and asserted required p-value and peak columns.

assertions.text: The DA test controls for fragment-depth variation
assertions.note: FindMarkers used latent.vars = nCount_peaks and test.use = LR.

assertions.text: A nonempty, parseable result table is written
assertions.note: The run wrote 147 rows with p_val, p_val_adj, and peak fields.

assertions.text: The Skill warns about peak-set double-dipping
assertions.note: The documented caveat remains present.

assertions.text: The output avoids causal TF claims from peak statistics
assertions.note: Interpretation remains association-level.

inputs.label: Documented chromVAR CLI workflow
inputs.note: The exact documented script invocation stopped before analysis: library(Signac) could not locate Signac in the designated private R library.
inputs.execution_note: run/05_documented_chromvar_invocation.ps1 executed the exact source script through the designated r.sh wrapper and exited nonzero with the recorded missing-package error. A library-exposed diagnostic process was safely stopped after consuming about 2.0 GB without producing an output artifact.

assertions.text: The documented chromVAR command starts with the designated audit environment
assertions.note: It fails at library(Signac) before reading the object.

assertions.text: The command produces the documented output RDS and differential CSV
assertions.note: No output files were written before failure.

assertions.text: The chromVAR path is reproducible by direct rerun
assertions.note: A direct rerun reproduces the same startup failure, not a result artifact.

assertions.text: The interpretation warns that motif enrichment is not single-TF causality
assertions.note: The surrounding Skill prose includes the required motif-family and occupancy caveats.

inputs.label: Single motif claimed as a causal TF
inputs.note: The direct Mode-A response rejected the requested causal conclusion, explaining paralogous motifs, presence versus occupancy, and the need for multiome expression or footprinting.
inputs.execution_note: Executed as a direct application of the documented chromVAR interpretation section; no external data or unsupported tool was claimed.

assertions.text: The response does not name one motif hit as a proven driver
assertions.note: It retains association-level wording.

assertions.text: The response explains motif-family ambiguity
assertions.note: Paralogous TF motifs are identified as a limitation.

assertions.text: The response offers an appropriate confirmation route
assertions.note: Multiome RNA and pseudobulk footprinting are offered.

assertions.text: No clinical or individual-level conclusion is made
assertions.note: The output remains research-method guidance.

inputs.label: Request to skip all QC filtering
inputs.note: The direct Mode-A response warns that skipping QC admits debris and low-quality cells, distorts the peak matrix, and should not be used as a blanket shortcut.
inputs.execution_note: Executed as a direct application of the QC Thresholds and Common Errors sections; response uses the documented data-quality caveats.

assertions.text: The response identifies the cost of omitting QC
assertions.note: It names empty droplets, debris, and spurious clusters.

assertions.text: The response does not endorse a blanket QC bypass
assertions.note: It recommends data-derived thresholds instead.

assertions.text: The response preserves the distinction between QC and doublet detection
assertions.note: It does not substitute one for the other.

assertions.text: The response remains non-diagnostic and research-scoped
assertions.note: No patient-specific interpretation is made.

key_strengths: The Signac TF-IDF/LSI path, per-component depth diagnosis, and depth-aware DA all executed on a realistic synthetic object.
The Skill gives unusually strong methodological boundaries for motif interpretation, peak-set circularity, gene activity, and QC.
The chromVAR migration replaced the removed wrapper with a public lower-level API and explicitly seeds background sampling.
No credential, destructive-command, or clinical-practice safety issue was found.

recommendations.title: Make run_chromvar.R load the designated R library
recommendations.problem: The documented direct invocation cannot load Signac in the named environment, so it produces none of its promised artifacts.
recommendations.root_cause: The moved standalone R script omitted the .libPaths() initialization used by audit scripts while r.sh only configures runtime DLL paths.
recommendations.fix: Add .libPaths(c('F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/single-cell-transcriptomics-analyst/R-lib', .libPaths())) before library() calls, then rerun the exact documented command twice and compare its CSV outputs.

recommendations.title: Remove the stale RunChromVAR name from the overview
recommendations.problem: The opening R workflow still instructs RunChromVAR() even though later text correctly says it was removed in Signac 1.17.0.
recommendations.root_cause: The overview was not updated when the detailed chromVAR section migrated to the new script.
recommendations.fix: Replace the overview wrapper name with the run_chromvar.R invocation or the lower-level chromVAR API sequence.

recommendations.title: Add concise escape-hatch guidance
recommendations.problem: The Skill lacks a dedicated stop or handoff section for unsupported framework environments and causal regulatory claims.
recommendations.root_cause: Out-of-scope boundaries are distributed across prose rather than collected for agent routing.
recommendations.fix: Add a short Escape Hatches subsection that points large Linux workflows to a supported environment and motif-to-TF causal questions to confirmatory multiome or footprinting analysis.
